l.i: Carmina: Romanis consulfit victima: noftro
Sanguine quaratur victoria, sanguine noftro
Placentur sani manes, placetur Erinnys.
Mox igitur prætextam armis imponere iuss-
us, Velatusque caput, mentoque innixus, & imis
Subiecto pedibus telo fortissimus heros
His se deuouit verbis, præfante ministro:
Iane, & tu custos Capitoli Iuppiter, audi,
Et gemini Romæ auctores, Mauorsque Quirine,
Et reliqua in noftris notissima numina fastis:
Vos etiam, o, manes Decii hæc audite precante.
Si qua premit patriam Nemesis, nunc vincere Romam
Crimina si qua vetant, Decius luat omnia solus.
Seruetur patria incolumis, pulsoque Latino,
Sublimes ducant Romani ex hoste triumphos.
Interea, collega, aciem patriamque tuere:
Ominor ecce fugam moriens mortemque Latinis.
Defierat: faciem lux protinus occupat ingens.
Qualis post noctis tenebras fulgore corusco
Emicat, & totum illustrat Sol aureus orbem.
Talis equo insiliens Decius sublimis habenas
Laxat, & in medios volat imperterritus hostes.
Illum fulgentemque armis, cinctúque Gabino,
Ipse admiratur Veseris, miratur & ipse
Iuppiter, & lauum tonat, audito omine lati
Prospiciunt Romani omnes, oculisque sequuntur,
Confusis attoniti facto. Iam tetra Latinus
Vertit, & aduentu Vnius mutata repente
Sors omnis: redeunt acies, animisque receptis,
Instat

page.notes: Marginal marks at right beside several lines (e.g. after "Quirine", "Romæ", "tonat") are reference signs, not transcribed. Doubtful: "Veseris" and "Quirine" as printed; "corusco" partly unclear; "sors omnis" line partly blurred. Verse lines are italic throughout.
